newsitem.title: UK: Forties crude pipeline shut for one hour Monday-BP.
newsitem.headline: Forties crude pipeline shut for one hour Monday-BP.

text.p: The million barrel per day North Sea Forties crude pipeline was closed down for about one hour on Monday morning due to a technical problem, operator British Petroleum said.
A spokesman said the pipeline was closed at 1045 local (0945 GMT) for an hour due to technical problems during maintenance at the Kinneil gas separation plant on the east Scottish coast.
"It was a very short-term problem," he said but gave no further details.
Crude throughput ran at an average 840,000 barrels per day over the previous 24 hours. BP said it would take about three hours for the pipeline to get back to previous flow levels.
Other operators said they had to shut in production at individual fields feeding the Forties stream while the line was down.
The BP spokesman said he did not expect the incident to impact on loading schedules.
Production problems at Enterprise Oil's Nelson field in the Forties system earlier this month caused the deferral of two July cargoes to August.
